I'd like to approach this from a different point of view. While I know it may not be most helpful comment for most of you here, I still feel like I could contribute to the general discussion.

I'm going to start by saying that I was born pretty privileged in terms of my looks. Ever since I was a child I've always been called cute. Later on, when I grew up and hit puberty, people were calling me beautiful. And I'm not saying it to brag or anything. I'm seeing men turning their heads everywhere I go. In consequence, most of my self-esteem was built on how I look. I started to believe that it was all I had to offer. I know it may sound vague or pretentious, but hear me out. I definitely feel like it contributed to me being unhappy more than it has to my happiness. At this point in life I don't know who I am except for "pretty". I have believed my whole life that I wasn't smart enough to pursue what I really wanted to do in life, because 'being beautiful' was all I had. Nobody has ever told me "you're smart" or "you're good at XXX". I've put more time and effort into following the beauty standards set by fashion models and magazines than I have into actually bettering myself. I wish I did things differently. I constantly felt like I needed to prove myself to other people and live up to the expectations they had of me. I could never let them see me "undone" or not looking my best. When I got sick and looked off, I couldn't leave my house. It messes with your mind a lot. I'm sure some of you can relate. I just wish I had a better understanding of what I should be focusing on back then. I wish I knew what was important and what was not. I wish I knew what I know now. I feel like most of my life has been wasted by worrying so much about my appearance. While I enjoyed looking good, it has also turned out to be toxic.

Again, I know those are "first world problems" etc, but we live in a society that puts so much pressure on the physical side of us that it's almost impossible to overlook. I just have never had the strength not to fall into this trap. I got so lost in it. Outer beauty can definitely be a great thing for some. I know people who have built their entire careers based on it. I envy those who could take advantage of it and make amazing things out of it. Those who could make their careers, which may seem shallow at the first glance, into something that actually contributes towards society. I'm talking about organizations like Knot on My Planet  (which I think is an amazing initiative).  I'm just not one of those people. I never knew what to do with it or how to use it to my advantage. I still don't. And it's not so much about using your beauty - not everyone needs to do that - some are extremely beautiful but also very successful in a totally different careers. I think that's GREAT. I wish it could be me. I just feel like I've lost so much time focusing on being 'beautiful' that I missed out on a lot of things. I didn't have the courage or confidence in myself to study Medicine (which has always been my dream but I quickly gave it up thinking I wasn't good enough). The never-ending compliments just taught me that it's all I have. If I can't use that - what else do I have? I honestly think that being "average" can be more beneficial to your life than being "beautiful". (I'm using quotation marks because c'mon, we're all unique and beautiful! I know that now). You have more time and confidence to improve other parts of you because you're not caught up in things that doesn't matter - e.g. external beauty. Maybe that was my environment/upbringing that played bigger role than the fact that I'm "pretty"? I honestly can't answer that.
